articles.title: Patch Tuesday, May 2026 Edition
articles.summary: CISA contractor yolo'd AWS GovCloud keys and agency secrets onto public GitHub because apparently 'security through obscurity' doesn't apply when you're literally the cybersecurity agency. Peak irony achieved.

articles.title: 23andMe inherits lawsuit over 'disturbing' DNA data breach
articles.summary: Critical RCE in Gogs remains unfixed since March while maintainers ghost the researcher who found it. Nothing says 'responsible disclosure' like radio silence and active exploit modules.

articles.title: Dutch cops wrest 17M devices from mystery botnet's clutches
articles.summary: 23andMe gets sued for downplaying their DNA breach while allegedly paying ransom to attackers. Your genetic privacy got sold faster than a startup's user data.

articles.title: ChatGPhish Vulnerability Turns ChatGPT Web Summaries Into a Phishing Surface
articles.summary: Palo Alto's PAN-OS auth bypass (CVE-2026-0257) is getting hammered in the wild. When your firewall becomes the front door, you're having a very bad time.

articles.title: 6 million Carnival Cruise customers’ data impacted amid hacker group’s slew of breaches
articles.summary: Disgruntled bug hunter promises 'bone shattering' 0-day drop after Microsoft 'humiliation.' Hell hath no fury like a security researcher scorned by corporate arrogance.

articles.title: Biden Sues DOJ to Block Release of Ghostwriter Audio in Classified Documents Probe
articles.summary: Hackers exploiting FortiClient EMS auth bypass to drop EKZ infostealer because nothing says 'enterprise security' like getting pwned through your own management console.

articles.title: More License Plate Reader Mission Creep: School Residency Verification, Background Checks, and Noise Complaints
articles.summary: Age verification schemes are privacy nightmares wrapped in 'think of the children' rhetoric. Lawmakers creating surveillance states while claiming to protect kids from seeing boobs online.

articles.title: 🔒 A Win for Encrypted Messaging | EFFector 38.10
articles.summary: Police are using license plate readers for everything except actual crime investigation—school residency checks, noise complaints, fishing expeditions. Mission creep or mission sprint?

articles.title: Microsoft Took a Step Toward Human Rights Accountability. Google and Amazon (and Others) Should Pay Attention!
articles.summary: EFF scores a win for encrypted messaging, keeping our digital conversations safe from government snoops and corporate data hoarders. End-to-end encryption remains undefeated.

articles.title: Alleged Kimwolf Botmaster ‘Dort’ Arrested, Charged in U.S. and Canada
articles.summary: Congress demands answers after CISA's contractor leaked government secrets like a sieve. When the cybersecurity agency can't secure its own shit, democracy weeps.
